runs.title: Continuity smoke test
runs.summary: The prior local runner still compiles and runs on Windows with GCC 16.1 and sorts 1,000 uint32 keys correctly. Not an evaluation of the goal.

runs.title: Viability review and repository reset
runs.summary: Judged the original goal (25% faster in 90% of a large benchmark matrix) very unlikely to be reached, replaced it with an open search for new mechanisms and archived the prior research.

runs.title: Record permutation headroom pilot
runs.summary: Gathering the payload takes 51–68% of an indirect sort of 64- and 128-byte records, so a permutation as cheap as a sequential copy would give about 1.3–1.4×. Enough room to try a candidate, with little margin.
runs.result: 1.29–1.40× estimated headroom; 5/8 cases ≥1.3× on both seeds
runs.baseline: fastest of vqsort + gather, x86-simd-sort + gather and pdqsort on rows

runs.title: Blocked record permutation probe
runs.summary: Rewriting and sorting descriptors and then moving the records in cache-sized tiles took 1.67–2.14× as long as the original gather phase. The probe measured those costs together. Gather with software prefetch won all 48 paired repetitions.
runs.baseline: fastest measured reference, including gather with software prefetch
opens: gather with software prefetch as the control to beat

runs.title: Page-remapped merge pilot
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.summary: Mapping pages instead of copying them pays off from 64 KiB extents upwards (4 KiB extents lose). In a merge only page-aligned slices qualify, which was 37.5% of the output when two runs overlap at the edges and 3–7% for bursty runs.
runs.result: 1.52–1.59× estimated for edge overlap; at most 1.08× for bursty runs

runs.title: Page-remapped merge candidate
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.summary: Mapping aligned input pages into the output beat the best fresh-output merge of two sorted runs of 128-byte records by 1.33–1.36×, and by 2.67× when 75% of the output was mapped. It lost to a merge into an already-touched buffer (0.36–0.74×) and regressed on bursty and interleaved runs (0.82–0.86×). Synthetic data only.
runs.result: 1.326–2.668× on edge-overlap runs (2/4 cases ≥1.3×, 0/4 ≥1.5× on both seeds)
runs.baseline: fastest merge into a fresh output
opens: frequency of mappable pages in real sorted batches

runs.title: GH Archive page coverage
runs.summary: All eight registered archive pairs had disjoint event-time ranges. Between 48.25% and nearly 100% of the modeled bytes can be remapped, so these inputs measure assembly of preordered ranges and leave overlap untested.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.result: 8/8 pairs passed 37.5% coverage; 0/8 had timestamp overlap
opens: timing against two bulk copies on the archive batch sizes

runs.title: Page remapping on GH Archive batch sizes
runs.summary: On eight disjoint pairs with batch sizes and order derived from GH Archive, remapping beat every fresh-output reference. It beat the resident-buffer references in the two cases where almost all pages could be mapped. Real overlapping arrivals remain untested.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.baseline: fastest of scalar, galloping bulk, hybrid and two-copy concatenation for fresh output; hybrid and two-copy concatenation for resident output
opens: test overlapping batches from a source with independent arrival and event clocks

runs.title: Record permutation by source band
runs.summary: Grouping reads by source band took about 23% longer on the primary batch. Preparing the groups and moving rows together took longer than reading ahead in the original layout.
runs.baseline: Fastest measured indirect sort with software prefetch

runs.title: Windows page remapping and first read
runs.summary: For 64 KiB blocks, Windows remapping and a first read took 2.21–2.54× the time of streaming copy and a first read. The first access to the new virtual addresses dominated even when larger blocks made the remap calls fast.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.baseline: AVX2 streaming copy plus first sweep into a reused output
closes: Windows placeholder remapping for the measured contract

runs.title: Stable rank inversion for four-record groups
runs.summary: Computing ranks and inverting them in AVX2 registers took 5–37% longer than the fastest direct SIMD reference on the primary batches. The extra work still cost time in the cache-resident control.
runs.idea: 5. Exact rank computation without data movement
runs.baseline: Best of the direct AVX2 compare-exchange network and shuffle lookup

runs.title: Page reuse in completed taxi-trip batches
runs.summary: Only one of twelve weekly pairs overlapped in pickup time. Four rows of that pair fell inside the overlap, and choosing the output offset did not increase its page reuse.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.result: 1/12 weekly pairs overlapped and 0/12 put at least 5% of rows in the overlap
closes: small seaborn taxi sample for overlapping merge timing
opens: dense completed-trip replay with substantial overlap
